content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Troubleshooting Split-Brain and Replication Lag in PostgreSQL"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"High availability (HA) architectures in PostgreSQL rely on robust replication mechanisms. However, network partitions and heavy write workloads can lead to severe operational challenges: split-brain scenarios and high replication lag. This tutorial covers the diagnostic and remediation steps required to resolve these issues safely."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding Replication Lag"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replication lag occurs when a standby server falls behind the primary instance in applying Write-Ahead Logs (WAL). You can monitor this in real-time by querying the replication statistics views."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"SELECT client_addr, state, sent_lsn, write_lsn, flush_lsn, replay_lsn, \npg_wal_lsn_diff(sent_lsn, replay_lsn) AS lag_bytes \nFROM pg_stat_replication;"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Mitigating Replication Lag"},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Increase max_parallel_apply_workers on the standby to speed up WAL application."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Tune wal_sender_timeout and max_wal_size to prevent premature WAL recycling on the primary."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Evaluate network bandwidth and disk I/O bottlenecks on the standby server."},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Diagnosing Split-Brain Risks"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"A split-brain scenario happens when two nodes believe they are the primary, accepting writes simultaneously and causing divergent data histories. This usually stems from misconfigured fencing mechanisms or network isolation."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"SELECT pg_is_in_recovery();"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"If both your designated primary and standby return 'f' (false) for the recovery status, you have an active split-brain."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Resolving Split-Brain and Re-syncing Standby"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"To resolve a split-brain, you must demote the erroneous node, preserve its timeline if possible, or re-initialize it as a standby using pg_rewind or a complete base backup."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"pg_rewind --target-server-target='host=primary_host port=5432 user=replicator' --source-server='host=standby_host port=5432 user=replicator'"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Always ensure your HA orchestrator (such as Patroni or repmgr) has fencing configured correctly using STONITH (Shoot The Other Node In The Head) principles to automatically prevent split-brain occurrences."}]
